activities.anchor: with a low blood pressure and a silent left chest
activities.caption: triage the panel — work the silent chest
activities.name: cpaSilentBranch

config.root: Triage by panel: respiratory rate high, blood pressure falling, and one side of the chest transmits no breath sound at all. The patient is not 'sick in general' — the panel is naming something specific. Work it:

start.text: The examination narrows it first: what occupies the space where sounds should be?

choices.label: Air — the lung has been pushed aside
choices.feedback: Pneumothorax: air in the pleural space separates lung from chest wall — percussion tympanic, breath sounds and fremitus absent.

choices.label: Fluid — the space is filled
choices.feedback: Large effusion (or haemothorax): dull to percussion, sounds absent, and the mediastinum can shift.

choices.label: The patient is anxious — nothing structural
choices.feedback: Anxiety does not silence a chest. Falling pressure with absent sounds is an emergency pattern — assess, image, act.

air.text: Tympanic percussion, absent sounds, falling pressure: tension physiology is on the table — decompression outranks everything else.

fluid.text: Dullness, absent sounds, decreased fremitus: the film will size it, and drainage follows the physiology, not the number alone.

anxious.text: The panel never supports ignoring a quiet chest — triangulate: examination, gas, imaging. Assessment is the therapy's aiming system.

config.why: The gas-exchange machinery reports status continuously, in numbers and signs; the foundational skill is reading the panel and knowing the physiology behind every needle — and no single value ever diagnoses.

activities.caption: order the breath, step by step
activities.name: cpaBreathOrder

config.prompt: From nose to elastic recoil — rebuild the path:
items: Air enters the conducting airways — trachea, bronchi, bronchioles — warmed, humidified, filtered, exchanging no gas
About 150 mL of anatomic dead space re-fills before anything fresh arrives
Fresh air reaches the roughly 300 million thin-walled alveoli wrapped in capillaries
Oxygen diffuses in and CO₂ diffuses out across a membrane under a micrometre thick
The whole exchange completes in about a quarter of a second
The diaphragm relaxes; elastic recoil pushes air back out
config.why: Contracting the diaphragm drops thoracic pressure so air flows in — which is why a patient whose lungs have lost elasticity (emphysema) must work to exhale.

activities.anchor: is the heart of respiratory pathophysiology
activities.caption: file the V/Q failures
activities.name: cpaVQSort

config.prompt: Perfusion without ventilation, or ventilation without perfusion — file each:

items.label: the body's partial fix: blood steered away from poorly ventilated regions

config.why: That partial fix is hypoxic vasoconstriction. The gas exposes which side failed — ventilation or perfusion — which is why V/Q matching sits at the centre of the specialty.

config.prompt: On the flat top of the S-shaped oxyhaemoglobin curve, saturation stays high until arterial O₂ tension falls below roughly what?
config.why: Below about 60 mmHg the curve turns steep — tissue-unloading territory. Acid, heat and CO₂ all shift the curve right (easier unloading), linking the two gases' transport.

activities.anchor: a patient hyperventilating on 100 mL of blood
activities.caption: true or false — the hyperventilation trap
activities.name: cpaHardJudge

statements.s: Breathing harder always raises PaO₂ meaningfully.
statements.why: Oxygen uptake is perfusion-limited and haemoglobin-limited; blood bypassing the alveoli is not fixed by moving more air.

statements.s: Ventilation moves CO₂ fast, while oxygen uptake is limited by perfusion and haemoglobin.
statements.why: That asymmetry is the physiology behind the trap — CO₂ responds to ventilation, oxygen does not, in shunt.

statements.s: A shunt patient breathing harder will raise PaO₂ only a little, at best.
statements.why: The bypassed blood never meets fresh air — that is what makes shunt oxygen-resistant.

statements.s: The asymmetry is why the ABG can separately implicate the lungs (CO₂) and the metabolism (HCO₃⁻).
statements.why: A diagnostic elegance the therapist works with every shift.

config.text: The gas reports four principal values — pH normal %%0%%, PaCO₂ %%1%% mmHg, HCO₃⁻ %%2%% mEq/L, plus PaO₂.
config.hint: Three ranges, in the order the gas reports them.

activities.anchor: The examination narrows the hypothesis before the imaging
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the four moves audited
activities.name: cpaExamSpot

config.prompt: One line of this exam summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Inspection: neck-muscle use and nostril flaring are distress signs; a barrel chest suggests hyperinflation.
Palpation: tactile fremitus increases over consolidated lung, decreases over fluid.
Percussion: hollow over normal lung, dull over consolidation or fluid, tympanic over pneumothorax.
Crackles are the sound of narrowed airways — a harsh cousin of the wheeze.
Auscultation: vesicular is normal; bronchial sounds are harsh and sit over consolidation.
config.correction: Crackles are fluid in the airways — oedema, pneumonia, fibrosis; wheezes are the narrowed-airway sound (asthma, COPD).
config.why: The added sounds also include the pleural friction rub — inflamed pleura grating. Dull percussion plus bronchial breath sounds plus crackles is pneumonia's signature long before the film.

activities.anchor: Labs complete the picture and cross-check the gas
activities.caption: pair each lab with what it flags
activities.name: cpaLabsMatch

config.prompt: The lab panel — pair each value with its question:

pairs.right: sets oxygen content — anaemia can leave breathlessness with normal saturations
points at cardiac causes of breathlessness
helps exclude embolism in low-risk patients
shapes infection stories, with WBC and CRP

config.why: Electrolytes travel with acid–base disorders too — chloride gaps, potassium shifts. The habit repeats: no single value diagnoses; the argument is triangulated.
